newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold gains as dollar supports bulls.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold gains as dollar supports bulls.

text.p: German shares held most of their gains on Wednesday afternoon, off earlier highs but supported by the unstoppable dollar and bullish news from Wall Street, where the Dow breached 8,000 points for the first time.
The IBIS DAX index stood at 4,214.04 points, up 74.36 points or 1.80 percent in afternoon trade, off earlier highs at 4,234.87 points.

"Dealers here are just as surprised as everyone else about the continued rise of the market. The environment is right, even though everyone is still waiting for the long-overdue correction," a Frankfurt trader said.
The market was holding steady above the 4,200-point threshold, which was penetrated for the first time earlier in the day.
Generally it was a good day for breaking psychological barriers, as the Dow Jones Industrial index also broke 8,000 points for the first time, before falling back after Eastman Kodak Co opened lower.
Underpinning the strength of the DAX was still the U.S. dollar, which traded at 1.7993/98 in afternoon trade.
Among shares on the move was Bayerische Vereinsbank, which was up over five percent in the afternoon.
Bayerische Vereinsbank was up 3.70 marks at 82 marks.
"There are no special reasons for this. A lot of it is probably down to the usual takeover speculation," said the trader.
The volume leaders in the afternoon were the banks and the chemical stocks, which traders attributed to positive sentiment in both sectors.
BASF AG led volumes, up 1.85 marks at 70.75 marks, while Bayer was up one mark at 75.50 marks and Hoechst was up 3.50 marks at 85.60.
Deutsche Bank was up 1.45 marks at 108.20 marks, Commerzbank was up 1.10 marks at 53.45 marks, while Dresdner was up 3.10 marks at 74.50 marks.
"There were good volumes across the board which helped all the major stocks, not just banks and chemicals, even if they were particularly favoured," a trader said.

Retailer Karstadt was up 39.40 marks at 680.50 marks, boosted by expectations that restructuring at the group would soon take hold, despite expectations that it could be dropped from the DAX in favour of Adidas.
